title: Escalation timebox, safety-net policies, and per-account feature sandboxes
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable protocol that lets high-value customers request accelerated roadmap work with explicit timeboxes and engineering safety-nets, while minimizing disruption to the main backlog and preserving delivery SLAs.

Why this matters: Top accounts occasionally need rapid feature variants or experiments. Current ad-hoc escalations create scope creep, unclear commit expectations, and make trade-offs invisible to other customers. We need a predictable path: fast-track requests => feature sandbox => measured canary => either merge into mainstream roadmap or retire.

Proposed approach:
1) Intake guardrail: a lightweight application form (CS + AE) that captures objective, requested SLAs, business impact, and rollback tolerance.
2) Timeboxed commitment: commit N sprints or M weeks (default 6 weeks) with a hard freeze date. After the timebox ends, deliverables must be either promoted, deferred with clear scope, or sunsetted.
3) Per-account sandboxing: provide an isolated runtime/config flag + dataset scope where we can field a customer-specific variant for testing. Sandboxes run on Dedicated or Private lanes where appropriate.
4) Safety-net policies: automated fallback routing and degradation rules (route to smaller model variant, throttle, or show a standardized failure banner) plus pre-agreed rollback playbooks.
5) Delegated approval matrix: Grant Product/CS a documented set of thresholds where they can greenlight timeboxed experiments; anything above threshold requires exec sign-off.
6) Metrics & exit criteria: success measured by adoption (DAU from account), latency/cost delta, error rate, and a qualitative CS score. Define pass/fail for promotion to mainline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form built and integrated into support HQ (link to doc below).
- Sandbox provisioning flow documented and validated with infra/eng (test job that spins up sandbox in < 8 hours).
- Safety-net runbook and rollback playbook written and reviewed by Reliability and Security.
- Delegation matrix approved by VP Product and Head of CS.
- Pilot with 2 strategic accounts completed, with clear go/no-go decisions documented.

Deliverables & owners:
- Intake form & CS playbook: Maya Fernandez (CS lead) + PM owner (Marcus Cole).
- Sandbox infra template & cost model: Eng infra lead (TBD, dependency ENG-1842).
- Rollback & safety-net runbooks: Reliability (ENG) + Security review.
- Pilot evaluation deck & recommendation: Marcus Cole

Links:
- Intake spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/ESCB-Intake-Form
- Sandbox infra proposal (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SandboxProposal
- Early cost model (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SandboxCostModel

Risks & open questions:
- Cost leakage from per-account sandboxes if left running indefinitely (mitigation: auto-terminate + cost quotas).
- Data isolation requirements for regulated customers may require Private deployment; needs SRE capacity planning.
- Delegation thresholds need legal/finance alignment for contractual commitments.

Next steps:
- Week 1: Finalize intake form and delegation matrix; get VP sign-off.
- Week 2-3: Build sandbox provisioning POC with ENG-1842.
- Week 4-6: Pilot with first account; collect metrics and iterate.
